clue.text: Consternation shown by retired man and woman

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name
May is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Dismay felt by a pensioner couple, a man and a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns only the man's name; two short names with no other help make this one tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a sudden feeling of alarm and distress, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Menial servant the setter has?

definitions.meaning: a drudge who does all the dull jobs
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge given all the lowly chores is called by this informal British term.

clue.text: Polish ambassador kept in Asian money

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the money word

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of several Asian countries, such as Japan
HE, His or Her Excellency, is the style of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy from Poland is paid in Asian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the noun for gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish here is the noun meaning a lustrous shine, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Island producing a sweet flavoured wine

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth, a sweet flavoured wine, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: An island that makes a sweet dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin and it' is a British drink of gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Rent room reportedly belonging to priests

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the words are heard not seen

parts.note: to rent is to hire; an attic is a room in the roof

explanation.surface: Rumour says a rented room is church property.
explanation.walkthrough: HIRE ATTIC, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieratic means of or relating to priests, as in the priestly Egyptian script.

clue.text: Come uninvited? One's not heartless and discourteous

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is the link 'has'

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle letter of the word not

parts.note: the word not itself, before its centre goes
discourteous means rude

explanation.surface: Someone turns up unasked, and is rude about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the O out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter where one has not been invited, so the definition fits.

clue.text: Stirring memories of newish skirts taken in

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, here inside the word for newish

parts.note: recent means fairly new
minis are miniskirts

explanation.surface: Fond memories of new short skirts being altered by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' plays on dressmaking, where a skirt is taken in; here it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent of a thing calls it to mind, stirring memories of it.

clue.text: Drink one by one? It's how some jokers behave

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means individually, one at a time

explanation.surface: Downing drinks one at a time, as practical jokers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Jokers who rib others act teasingly, in a mocking playful manner, so this adverb describes them.

clue.text: Where our betters show envy, say, in company?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: envy is an example of a sin, so a sin

explanation.surface: A place where social superiors display envy in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betters' means people who bet, not superiors.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling house, where people who place bets turn up.

clue.text: Dandy film container

parts.note: a buck is an old word for a fashionable man
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A dandy's film is reduced to a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket is a pail, an open container for carrying water.

clue.text: Good king rejected gibe about a relative

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the king's letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Edward Rex, stands for a king
a taunt is a gibe

explanation.surface: A virtuous monarch dismisses a jibe about a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, so she is a family relation.

clue.text: Niggardly son's resources

parts.note: niggardly means stingy, mean
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's is the link 'has'

explanation.surface: A miserly son's assets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's means are their money and resources, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Where Bruce won right to dip into bakery products

indicators.note: to dip into means to go inside the bakery words

parts.note: a bannock is a Scottish flat loaf and a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A Scottish hero won the right to dunk his bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce beat the English at Bannockburn in 1314; R goes into BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bannockburn was the 1314 battle where Robert the Bruce defeated the English army, so it is the place.

clue.text: Where a jumped-up cow went, cock-a hoop

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the cow jumped above the night sky's satellite

explanation.walkthrough: 'jumped-up' usually means upstart, but here the cow literally jumped.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for delighted and also the cow's route in the rhyme.

clue.text: Possibly Jamaica's trendy name

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island's fashionable name.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamaica Inn is the Daphne du Maurier novel set at a Cornish inn; 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is a famous Cornish tavern, an example of a pub or hostelry.

clue.text: Drop objection to listeners

indicators.note: to listeners means as heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: dissent is disagreement or objection

explanation.surface: Withdraw an objection to what the audience hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall, so drop as a noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Understaffed, editor's fore gone rapid writing

indicators.note: fore gone, ie foregone, means given up, so the editor's letters are lost

parts.note: short-handed means lacking enough staff
ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: With too few staff, the editor gave up on fast note-taking.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'foregone' over a line break; removing ED from SHORTHANDED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a system of abbreviated symbols for writing fast, eg in dictation.

clue.text: Flying officer?

parts.note: an RAF rank seems meant, but it is a flag that flies and also a junior naval officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying officer' looks like the RAF rank; really it joins a flag that flies and a junior US naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is both a flag flown on a ship and a junior naval officer rank.

clue.text: Like travels disrupting one's days?

indicators.note: disrupting means throwing into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as the letters of the word ones

explanation.surface: Some trips that throw a person's calendar into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Odyssean describes long wandering journeys, like those of Homer's hero Odysseus.

clue.text: Harry's agent retreats without going too far

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the agent's letters wrap round
retreats means goes back, so the agent's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
OTT, over the top, means going too far

explanation.surface: A boy wizard's representative pulls back before overstepping the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' reverses the agent, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. Harry is the boy wizard of J K Rowling's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry's surname in the J K Rowling stories completes the wizard's name, so the possessive points to it.

clue.text: Publicity around City is initially rather weak

indicators.note: around means the outer letters surround the City abbreviation
initially means the first letter of rather is taken

parts.note: lame means feeble or weak
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Media attention for the City is said to be rather feeble at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postal district is a crossword staple for 'City'; 'around' wraps the rest round it, and 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclame is French-derived for publicity or self-promotion.

clue.text: Drunk sees London feature in black and white

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for black and white

parts.note: pied means patched black and white, like a magpie
the London Eye is the big wheel on the South Bank

explanation.surface: A drunk spots a London landmark in monochrome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is only a link; the landmark is the big wheel on the Thames, slipped in before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal slang for intoxicated, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Unsuitable memorial for a dentist?

parts.note: a commemorative tablet shares its name with the film on teeth dentists remove

explanation.definitionFit: A plaque is a commemorative tablet, and also the deposit dentists scrape off teeth.

clue.text: Tough East Ender going over Arctic plain

indicators.note: going over means turning backwards here, in a down clue upwards

parts.note: a hard nut, said by a Cockney who drops the H as 'ard nut

explanation.surface: A hard man from East London crosses the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders (Cockneys of East London) drop their Hs, so a tough guy is an 'ard nut; reversed it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic regions.

clue.text: Posh officer in business during previous month

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An upper-class officer goes into commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Ult., short for ultimo, is commercial jargon for last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ult'.

clue.text: Circe, for example, regarding ship with delight

indicators.note: with here means the delight word goes alongside, in front of the others

parts.note: to enchant is to delight
re means regarding
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: The sorceress is pleased about a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of Circe; 'with' means the delight word comes first and the rest follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe was the sorceress in the Odyssey who turned men into swine, an example of a witch.

clue.text: The Spanish duke capturing an African mammal

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, here around an

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish duke catches an African beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, so it is an example of a mammal.

clue.text: Old king possibly backing stars

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch maybe supports celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OCARD to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco, the Dragon, is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Go over film, losing contact on the way?

definitions.text: Go over film, losing contact on the way?

parts.words: Go over film, losing contact on the way?
parts.note: a car skimming on a film of water loses grip on the road

explanation.definitionFit: To aquaplane is to skid when tyres ride on water and lose road contact.

clue.text: US writer and some of his output? Not half

indicators.note: not half means losing half its letters, here the back three

explanation.surface: An American writer and part of his work, but only half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: His output is POETRY; halved it leaves the name of Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American author of tales and poems such as The Raven.

clue.text: Composer's study in this part of France

indicators.note: in means placed inside the composer's name

parts.note: Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia; his name with the possessive S
a den is a study

explanation.surface: A composer's study in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a forested region of north-east France and Belgium.

clue.text: Sort of impact Charles I didn't have ultimately

definitions.meaning: describes a collision where two things meet front to front
King Charles I was beheaded in 1649, so at the end his head was off

explanation.walkthrough: Charles I of England was beheaded, so at the last he lacked this.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on collision is front to front, and the beheaded king lost his head.
